column1: # Reconciler skip-list — env/package pairs the reconciler should NOT keep retrying.
# aarch.science's gaps differ from aarchbio's (DESIGN D2/D3). aarchbio's unit is a
# single bioconda tool that may have "no arm64 build". Here the unit is a curated
# ENV, and a gap is a package we'd want in an env that EITHER won't solve on arm64
# conda-forge OR solves-but-won't-assemble/import on arm64 (the D3 failure mode —
# the subtle one). When such a package blocks an env, record it here so the daily
# reconciler stops re-trying a known dead-end, and document it in GAPS.md.
# Two tiers (mirrors aarchbio):
#   wontfix  — genuine dead-end; never retry (only a human edit removes it).
#   stuck    — real chance of an upstream fix (conda-forge feedstock re-enables
#              arm64, an ABI bug is fixed); skip the DAILY run but re-check every
#              <revisit_days>.
# Columns (tab-separated):  package  tier  revisit_days  reason
# (revisit_days is ignored for wontfix; use 0. `package` is the conda-forge package
#  name; prefix with `env:` to skip a whole env spec instead.)
# Edit this file to add/remove entries. The reconciler reads it each run.
# STATUS: 2 entries (as of 2026-08). The geo/climate/point-cloud/comp-chem head is
# still gap-free on conda-forge linux-aarch64 — both entries below came from scoping
# the `dft` env, which is where this catalog first met packages arm64 can't take:
# one runtime-download dead-end (whitebox) and one MPI-flavor collision (abinit).
# See GAPS.md for the full record and the upstream-contribution roadmap.
# --- wontfix: genuine dead-ends ---
whitebox
column4: conda-forge pkg downloads a precompiled WhiteboxTools_linux_amd64 binary from the network at runtime — wrong arch for arm64 (needs emulation) + runtime fetch; both violate native/no-emulation/verifiable. Excluded from `pointcloud`; richdem covers terrain/hydrology natively.

column1: # --- stuck: arm64 blocked with a real chance of upstream fix ---
abinit
column4: Third gap kind (MPI-flavor conflict), not a solve- or assemble-gap: abinit 10.0.3 HAS a linux-aarch64 build and solves standalone (59 pkgs), but only against MPICH — conda-forge ships no openmpi variant for it on aarch64. conda-forge permits one MPI implementation per env, so it cannot coexist with the OpenMPI-flavored gpaw in `dft`. Forcing the env to MPICH instead regresses the whole stack (gpaw 25.7.0 -> 23.9.1, python 3.14 -> 3.12, libxc 7.1.2 -> 6.2.2, elpa 2025.06 -> 2021.11), so OpenMPI wins and abinit is excluded. Fixable upstream: add an openmpi variant to conda-forge/abinit-feedstock for linux-aarch64. Revisit quarterly.
